answer: Cross-epoch behaviour fingerprinting. Each identity's task choices and counterparties each epoch are hashed into a compact onyx digest stored with prior epochs. At epoch boundaries an agent must reproduce a digest matching its own history within a set tolerance; mismatches trigger a hold on payouts until reconciled. Sybils pay a per-identity continuity cost: each fake must sustain consistent behaviour across many epochs, passing a prism of cross-checks, before it earns anything. Rotating identities forfeits accumulated history and starts below the velvet threshold where rewards unlock,
